full_judgment:
2. The present plaintiff-petitioner along with some others instituted the Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Chirirbandar, Dinajpur for a declaration that the preliminary decree as well as the final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 are illegal, ineffective and inoperative, making allegations to the effect that summons and notices of that partition suit were not served upon them, that Dhali Bibi the plaintiff of that partition suit had no subsisting interest in the divisible land, that the purchasers were not made parties in that partition suit and that the defendants who were of unsound mind and were minors were not represented properly in that partition suit. 

 3. That Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 was contested by saham-praying defendants of Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 by filing written statement. The case of the contesting defendants was that the summons and notices of that Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 were duly served upon the defendants and the suit was decreed on contest and the Advocate Commissioner partitioned the property and prepared the saham after serving notices upon the defendants duly and the preliminary decree was made final lawfully as no objection was filed against the Advocate Commissioner's report and that the final decree was executed by filing Partition Execution Case No. 1 of 1988 and possession of land was delivered on 28.03.1988 and that Dhali Bibi has been possessing the suit Land on the strength of her right and title. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties, decreed that Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 holding only that in the Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 the present plaintiffs were not served with the summons and notices. Against that judgment of the trial court the contesting defendants preferred Other Appeal No. 53 of 1991 before the learned District Judge, Dinajpur, which was ultimately heard and disposed of by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dinajpur. The appellate court dismissed the appeal, affirming the judgment of the trial court making observation to the effect that the plaintiffs were able to prove their case that they were not informed about that partition suit and that the trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the plaintiffs, rightly declared the preliminary decree and the final decree of the Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 illegal and inoperative. 

 8. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has argued that both the courts of fact, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the, plaintiffs, found that the summons and notices, of the original partition suit were not served upon the plaintiffs and consequently both the courts rightly found the preliminary decree as well as the final decree passed in that Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 illegal. That the trial court being the first court of fact and the appellate court below being the final court of facts their concurrent findings as to non-service of summons upon the defendants in the original partition suit cannot be interfered by the revisional court in the absence of any misreading or non-reading or misinterpretation of the evidence on record by those two courts below. The learned Advocate has argued that the High Court Division has committed illegality in setting aside the concurrent findings of the courts of fact. The learned Advocate has argued further that in this suit for declaring the judgment and decree of the earlier partition suit illegal the onus was upon the contesting defendants to prove that summons and notices of the partition suit were duly served upon the plaintiffs of the present suit, but the contesting defendants did not take any step or initiative to discharge that onus and in the circumstances, the evidence of the P.Ws. were sufficient to prove that the summons and notices of the original partition suit were not served upon them. 

 11. It appears that before the trial court seven witnesses were examined from the side of the plaintiffs all of whom were defendants in the original partition suit. These 7 P.Ws. deposed before the court to the effect only that they did not get summons and notices of the original partition suit. Save and except the evidence of these 7 P.Ws. who are most interested witnesses the plaintiffs did not or could not adduce any other evidence or facts or material to substantiate their allegation that the summons and notices of the original partition suit were not served upon them and these were suppressed collusively. It appears that the trial court and also the appellate court relying on this evidence of the P.Ws. only declared the preliminary and final decree passed in that partition suit illegal. 

 12. But the High Court Division, on careful and meticulous examination of the evidence and materials on record, pointed out that no necessary evidence or materials were produced before the courts below to substantiate the allegation of non-service of summons and notices; that neither the record of Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 was proved before the courts below, inn the service return of that partition suit was admitted into evidence for the purpose of proving this allegation of non-service of summons and notices. The High Court Division, on consideration of the evidence on record, observed also that the evidence of P.Ws. failed to make out any case of collusion in obtaining the preliminary decree and final decree passed in that partition suit. The High Court Division further, detected that the defendant No. 1 of that partition suit named Badiuzzaman along with some other defendants submitted written statement in that partition suit and this defendant No. 1 Badiuzzaman is the full brother of the plaintiff No. 1 of the present Other Class Suit No. 43 of 1989 and he has also deposed in that suit as P. W.2 in favour of the plaintiffs. On consideration of these facts and circumstances and the evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2-which have been quoted in the impugned judgment of the High Court Division the High Court Division made comment to the effect that this P.W.2 Badiuzzaman, in fact, filed this present suit setting up his sister as plaintiff. 

 13. On going through the judgments of both the courts of facts we do not find any wrong in the above findings of the High Court Division. From the judgment of the courts below it appears that in the original partition suit the defendant No. 1 Badiuzzaman (who deposed in the present suit as P. W.2) along with some other defendants submitted written statement and this very fact has not been denied by this defendant No. 1 while deposing in this present suit for setting aside the decree of that earlier partition suit as P.W.2. In the circumstances where the own brother of the plaintiff No. 1 of the present suit got summons and notices of the earlier partition suit and also appeared in that partition suit and filed written statement and where, admittedly, some other defendants also contested in that partition suit and prayed saham, it is hard to believe that the other defendants of that partition suit-who are full sister and other close relations of the contesting defendants did not get summons and notices of that partition suit or did not know about that partition suit. 

 14. In this circumstance the mere statements of the P.Ws. that they did not get summons and notices of the original partition suit are not sufficient at all for setting aside the judgment and decree passed by a court of law. When a judgment and decree is passed by court of law it is presumed that this judgment and decree was passed in accordance with law by following all the requirements of law so long it is not proved by cogent evidence that these judgment and decree were obtained collusively suppressing the summons and notices. In the present case the preliminary decree as well as the final decree of Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 was passed by a competent court of law. So the onus to prove this preliminary and final decree collusive or illegal was on the plaintiffs of the present suit who alleged the same. But the plaintiffs of this present suit could not produce any evidence at all to prove any collusion or fraud in obtaining the impugned decree of the partition suit. They did not take any step or initiative to bring the record of the Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984 before the trial court for the purpose of proving that the summons and notices were not issued and served or these were suppressed Collusively. None of the witnesses named in the service return of that partition suit also was produced before the trial court by the plaintiffs to deny the service of summons and notices in his presence and thereby to support the plaintiffs case that the summons and notices of the original partition Suit were not actually served upon them. In the circumstances, the mere assertion of the plaintiffs that they did not get any summons and notices of the partition suit was not at all sufficient for holding that actually the summons and notices of that partition suit were not served upon the plaintiffs of the present suit specially in the circumstances where it was sufficiently disclosed before the trial court that the own brother of the plaintiff No. 1 and some other defendants of that partition suit got summons and notices of that partition suit and they also appeared in that partition suit, filed written statement and contested. 

 15. In the circumstances the High Court Division rightly found that the plaintiffs of the present suit could not prove their case that the preliminary and final decree passed in the Partition Suit No.194 of 1984 were obtained collusively by suppressing summons and notices. The High Court Division rightly observed also that the courts below without applying judicial mind set aside the hard-earned preliminary and final decree passed in Partition Suit No. 194 of 1984.
